clock.problem: seeded rows carry the server's real creation time (November 2026 or later), which lies AFTER the frozen browser clock: every relative time ('3 days ago') would render as a negative or nonsense age
clock.rule: until a seed can back-date rows, every element that renders a time derived from the server is a mask ([data-relative-time], time). Proposed fix for ours: the seed door accepts created_at for the fixture workspace only (a plan and a gate are needed - not designed here). For references: mask.

rules: product-neutral: no product, vendor, model or place name appears in any text; a model is 'model-a', 'model-b'
every text is fixed and ASCII; every name is fixed; nothing is random and nothing is generated by a model at seed time
all assistant text in the fixture is typed by the seed (posted as the assistant where the product allows, else as the second person) - a live model reply is never part of a fixture
money is in one currency with fixed amounts; the currency code is a parameter of the seed (default USD) so a product that only knows one currency can still hold it
the fixture's hash = sha256 of this file's canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace); it is written into every capture

stubModel.what: one OpenAI-compatible endpoint on loopback that always answers a chat request with the same fixed text for the same prompt (a lookup of fixture.questions -> fixture.answers; anything else -> answers.default), with fixed token counts and no delay
stubModel.why: no provider is configured on any reference and staging has no model, so today no conversation screen can show an assistant reply and J1, J4, J8, J9 stop at the first send. A stub makes replies identical across products and runs, and costs nothing.
